title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: THE BIG HANDS
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Rusty Delgado, thirty-three, a pipeline welder in Odessa, Texas.
Rusty is six foot five, with hands like baseball mitts.
This fall, he decided to knit a baby blanket.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE YARN SHOP
segments.author: Amelia Earhart
lines: His wife Marisol was expecting their first baby, a girl, in March.
Rusty's Nana Pearl, eighty-eight, knitted his baby blanket. Now her hands were too stiff.
He sat outside the yarn shop for twenty minutes. Then he remembered a card from Amelia Earhart:
Adventure is worthwhile in itself.
He walked in and joined the Tuesday night knitting circle.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE NEEDLES
segments.quote: Mishaps are like knives, that either serve us or cut us, as we grasp them by the blade or the handle.
segments.author: James Russell Lowell
lines: The needles looked like toothpicks in his hands.
He squeezed them so hard he poked his thumb. Twice.
Opal, seventy-nine, the circle's leader, read him a line from the American writer James Russell Lowell:
Mishaps are like knives, that either serve us or cut us, as we grasp them by the blade or the handle.
So Rusty loosened his grip. Finally, the yarn moved.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE LUNCH BREAK
segments.quote: Great spirits have always encountered violent opposition from mediocre minds.
segments.author: Albert Einstein
lines: At lunch on the job site, Rusty pulled out his knitting.
The crew laughed so hard one guy dropped his burrito.
Rusty just smiled and quoted Albert Einstein:
Great spirits have always encountered violent opposition from mediocre minds.
Two weeks later, his foreman quietly asked for a beanie. In orange.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE HOLE
segments.quote: Patience and perseverance have a magical effect before which difficulties disappear and obstacles vanish.
segments.author: John Quincy Adams
lines: One night, Rusty found a hole. A dropped stitch, ten rows back.
Three weeks of work. He almost threw it in the trash.
Opal showed him how to pull the rows out, and read a line from President John Quincy Adams:
Patience and perseverance have a magical effect before which difficulties disappear and obstacles vanish.
So Rusty knitted them again, one row every night.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE EARLY ARRIVAL
segments.quote: Trust yourself. You know more than you think you do.
segments.author: Benjamin Spock
lines: Then the baby came three weeks early. The blanket was not finished.
At the hospital, Rusty held tiny Rosie and froze. I don't know how to do this, he said.
A nurse smiled and quoted the famous baby doctor Benjamin Spock:
Trust yourself. You know more than you think you do.
At three in the morning, in the hospital chair, he finished the last row.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE BLANKET
segments.quote: Blessed is the influence of one true, loving human soul on another.
segments.author: George Eliot
lines: The blanket was crooked and lumpy. Rosie did not care.
Rusty video called Nana Pearl in Abilene and held it up.
Nana wiped her eyes and said a line from the English novelist George Eliot:
Blessed is the influence of one true, loving human soul on another.
Now the Tuesday knitting circle has three welders in it.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Try something new. Loosen your grip. Ignore the laughing. Fix it. Trust yourself. Love out loud.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Try something new. Loosen your grip. Ignore the laughing. Fix your mistakes. Trust yourself. Love out loud.
I tried knitting once. I made a sweater with three arms. I'm still looking for the third person.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
